data.title: Low-Temperature Fatigue Root-Cause Analysis of Mild Steel Welded Conveyor Frames in Chilled Food Environments
data.markdown:
## The problem
AutomVoj a.d. has replaced 14 welded mild steel conveyor frame assemblies under warranty this year after cracking at the crossmember-to-stringer weld joints in 2–6 °C cold stores over an 18-month period. The failure cannot be reproduced in their workshop because all structural tests are conducted at room temperature.

## Research questions
1. By what mechanism(s) does thermal cycling between ambient shutdown conditions and the 2–6 °C operating range combine with belt-induced vibration loading to initiate and propagate cracking in the crossmember-to-stringer weld joints of mild steel hollow-section frames?
2. To what extent do the current weld procedure, filler metal selection, and joint design contribute to low-temperature fatigue sensitivity after approximately 18 months of continuous service?

## Plan
| Year | Work | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Forensic metallurgy on failed frames; in-service logging of vibration and thermal cycles on one conveyor line for 200 hours; build and correlate an as-welded FE model. | Quantified service load spectrum and a validated FE model that reproduces the crack-initiation stress field. |
| 2 | Synthesise measured load spectrum for servo-hydraulic fatigue tests at 2 °C and 6 °C on original-procedure weld mock-ups; use DIC and hole-drilling to monitor crack initiation and residual stress relaxation. | Reproduced failure with a documented cycles-to-initiation number; mechanistic explanation linking thermal cycles, vibration, and joint design. |
| 3 | Parametric FE sweeps of joint geometry, filler metals, and post-weld treatmen… [2506 chars cut]
data.namedPublication: Fatigue Crack Propagation in Fillet-Welded S355 Steel Under Variable-Amplitude Block Loading
data.candidate: A mechanical or materials engineer with a strong experimental mechanics background and finite element simulation skills, comfortable working on an industrial shop floor and in a low-temperature test lab.
researchQuestions: By what mechanism(s) does thermal cycling between ambient shutdown conditions and the 2–6 °C operating range combine with belt-induced vibration loading to initiate and propagate cracking in the crossmember-to-stringer weld joints of mild steel hollow-section frames?
To what extent do the current weld procedure, filler metal selection, and joint design contribute to low-temperature fatigue sensitivity after approximately 18 months of continuous service?

plan.work: Forensic analysis of failed field samples and construction of a representative FE model. Characterise base and weld materials via metallography and hardness mapping. Instrument an in-service conveyor to capture 200 hours of vibration and thermal-cycle data.
plan.result: Quantified service load spectrum (strain amplitudes, frequencies, temperature profiles) and a validated as-welded FE model identifying primary stress concentration zones.

plan.work: Replicate failure in a controlled lab environment using the −60 °C servo-hydraulic machine: apply synthesised block loading and thermal cycling to weld mock-ups. Measure residual stress evolution with hole-drilling, and monitor crack initiation with DIC.
plan.result: Reproduced failure with documented cycles-to-initiation and propagation rates; direct comparison of lab crack morphologies with field cracks.

plan.work: Parametric redesign campaign (joint geometry, filler alloy, post-weld treatment) with FE simulation and validation testing. Produce a revised welding procedure specification and performance test it under accelerated life conditions.
plan.result: Qualified revised welding and design procedure that demonstrates at least a 5x improvement in predicted fatigue life under the service spectrum.

company: Failed frame assemblies with known service history (SYN-C003-CH1-FAILURES), photographs, and site measurements.
Unrestricted access to an operational conveyor line for long-term vibration and temperature instrumentation.
Welding shop, fabrication capability, and senior welding engineers for producing test mock-ups and implementing new procedures.
faculty: Servo-hydraulic fatigue testing capacity with an environmental chamber capable of −60 °C for low-temperature cyclic loading (SYN-PUB-04474).
Full-field strain measurement by Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and residual stress expertise including simulation and hole-drilling method (R0365 equipment access).
Published competence in variable-amplitude block loading fatigue and the interaction of mechanical and thermal cycling on structural steel welds (SYN-PUB-04472, SYN-PUB-04475).

data.whyThisPair: AutomVoj a.d. has a recurring structural failure they cannot reproduce at room temperature, and Bojan Erić has a dedicated research line on low-temperature fatigue of welded steel joints with direct access to the required servo-hydraulic and thermal cycling equipment. His publication 'Fatigue Crack Propagation in Fillet-Welded S355 Steel Under Variable-Amplitude Block Loading' (SYN-PUB-04472) is a direct methodological precursor: it addresses the same joint class under realistic service spectra. His experimental study on cruciform joints at −40 °C (SYN-PUB-04474) and work on mechanical-thermal interaction (SYN-PUB-04475) provide the precise framework to test AutomVoj's hypothesis that thermal cycling plus vibration is the root cause.

agreedUpFront.ip: AutomVoj a.d. retains ownership of the final frame design and welding procedure specifications developed for its product line. The Faculty of Technical Sciences retains ownership of the experimental method and generalised fatigue assessment framework. Jointly developed FE models require mutual consent for disclosure.

risks: Failure mode cannot be reproduced in the lab within the project timeline because an unrecognised environmental factor (e.g., in-situ condensation-driven corrosion fatigue, not just thermal and mechanical cycling) dominates the cracking mechanism. Mitigation: forensics and site instrumentation in Year 1 must characterise potential corrosion fatigue before synthesising the lab test plan.
In-service instrumentation on a customer site is vetoed by the end user, delaying load spectrum acquisition.

The current mild steel base material has such poor low-temperature toughness that no realistic weld procedure modification provides sufficient life improvement, forcing a material upgrade that requires a costly full frame redesign.
unverified: The exact grade of mild steel hollow section used by AutomVoj is not provided, so the compatibility with Erić's S355 and low-alloy steel experience is assumed based on his keyword 'structural steel'.
AutomVoj's specific PLC and drive configurations and the resulting vibration frequencies on the conveyor belts are not stated and must be measured or provided during Year 1.
The name and exact capacity of the 'DIC setup' for strain measurement are not detailed in the researcher's profile.

data.title: Field-level precipitation estimation for rainfall-index insurance in Vojvodina using multi-source data

## The problem
OsiguroMi’s parametric crop product triggers payouts when the nearest official meteorological station records rainfall below a contractual threshold, but the station can be up to 30 km away, leading to unjustified payouts or missed claims (C004-CH1). A spatial rainfall estimate that works at the field scale is needed without replacing the regulatory framework.

## Research questions
1. How can satellite precipitation estimates, dense private gauge networks, and official station data be fused to produce a daily 1 km rainfall grid that reduces basis risk relative to the nearest-station threshold alone?
2. What is the spatial transferability of bias-correction factors derived from a 140-point network to operational index insurance triggers across Vojvodina parcels?

| Year | Work | Result |
|------|------|--------|

| 3 | Execute pre-agreed performance protocol; shadow-trigger integration in the API; regulatory documentation. | Production-ready API endpoint returning parcel-scale drought status, with measured false-payout improvement over the baseline. |

data.title: Separating guessing from learning in browser-based math games for primary schools: a three-year industrial PhD proposal

Teachers using Zrenjanin Game Works’ math games cannot determine whether a child is answering correctly by understanding the material or by rapid, random clicking. Clickstream logs for 4,200 students exist (2022–23 and 2023–24 school years), but the company lacks a method to separate genuine learning from guessing.

Build a hand-labelled set of at least 200 student–session pairs using teacher interviews and synthetic generation. Apply logistic regression and HMMs to distinguish guesser versus solver sessions.

## The problem
AutomVoj a.d. is experiencing premature weld joint cracking at the crossmember-to-stringer connections of their mild steel conveyor frames after about 18 months of continuous operation in customer cold stores operating between 2 °C and 6 °C. 3. Can a practical, FE-based structural integrity assessment method be developed to predict the service life of the redesigned joints?

data.title: Root-cause analysis and mitigation of low-temperature fatigue cracking in welded conveyor frames for cold-store operation
data.markdown:
## The problem
AutomVoj a.d. has been replacing welded mild-steel conveyor frames under warranty because crossmember-to-stringer fillet welds crack after approximately 18 months in cold stores operating between 2 °C and 6 °C. Fourteen complete assemblies have been replaced this year alone C003-CH1. The company cannot reproduce the failure in its workshop because all load tests are conducted at room temperature, and it suspects that thermal cycling, condensation and belt vibration act together to drive a damage mechanism that ambient testing misses C003-CH1.

## Research questions
1. What is the dominant damage mechanism that drives crack initiation in the mild-steel crossmember-to-stringer fillet welds when subjected to the combined effect of sustained vibration, condensation-driven corrosion, and thermal cycling between 2 °C and ambient?
2. Which combination of weld geometry, filler material or post-weld treatment can reliably extend the crack-initiation life beyond a five-year continuous cold-store duty, verified by a low-temperature block-loading fatigue test?

## Plan
| Year | Work | Result |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | Characterise as-built welds (macro-sections, residual stress via XRD), run 5 constant-amplitude fatigue tests at +2 °C with condensing humidity, build and calibrate a full-frame Abaqus FE model with DIC. | Validated FE model (strain within 15 %); quantified residual stress map; S–N data point from ≥ 5 valid specimens. |
| 2 | Capture vibration service logs, design a block-loading spectrum, test three improved joint variants inside the climate chamber … [3600 chars cut]

plan.work: Characterise the as-built frame: record weld profiles (macro-sections, toe radii, undercut) and measure residual stress by X-ray diffraction on three production frames and on the two failed frames in storage. Run five constant-amplitude fatigue crack-growth tests on extracted weld specimens inside the climate chamber at +2 °C, condensing humidity. Build a coupled thermo-mechanical Abaqus FE model of the bolted frame assembly and calibrate it with DIC strain fields from a cold-room load test.

plan.work: Design a block-loading spectrum from vibration logs captured on a customer line in Hungary. Run spectrum fatigue tests on standard and three improved joint variants (changed filler, toe grinding, PWHT) inside the climate chamber at +2 °C under condensing conditions. Use fracture-mechanics crack-growth prediction (NASGRO) parametrised with low-temperature da/dN data.
plan.result: Ranking of the three countermeasure variants by fatigue life extension factor. One variant selected for full-frame validation showing ≥3× life improvement over the current design in the block-spectrum test.

plan.work: Fabricate two full conveyor-frame modules with the winning joint design at the AutomVoj workshop. Commission a six-month accelerated durability test on the university servo-hydraulic rig inside the climate chamber, applying the block spectrum with daily thermal cycles between −5 °C and +25 °C. Derive an inspection interval and draft a revised welding procedure specification.
plan.result: Validated inspection interval (e.g., first non-destructive examination at 30 months). Draft WPS approved by the chief engineer. PhD thesis submitted.

faculty: Servo-hydraulic fatigue machine, climate chamber operational to −60 °C, 3D DIC system (Aramis) and Abaqus FE licences (R0365).

Proven protocols for low-temperature fatigue testing and residual-stress measurement on welded structural steel, and direct supervision by a researcher who already studies interaction of mechanical cyclic loading and thermal cycling on fatigue life of butt-welded structural steel plates (SYN-PUB-04475).

Bojan Erić's group has just published 'Low-Cycle Fatigue Behaviour of Cruciform Welded Joints at −40 °C: An Experimental Study' (SYN-PUB-04474) and 'Interaction of Mechanical Cyclic Loading and Thermal Cycling on Fatigue Life of Butt-Welded Structural Steel Plates' (SYN-PUB-04475), which together demonstrate that his lab already runs precisely the low-temperature cyclic tests with DIC instrumentation that the company lacks. No other faculty in the region combines a climate chamber to −60 °C, a servo-hydraulic rig, and a decade of fracture-mechanics modelling on welded steel grades. For the company, this is the fastest path to a weld procedure that survives a cold-store warranty period; for the researcher, it is a direct industrial validation of his group's laboratory methods on a real, high-consequence structure.

agreedUpFront.ip: Methods (FE modelling protocols, DIC measurement procedures, fatigue-life prediction scripts) are owned by the Faculty and may be published after review. Physical test rigs, jigs and the final welding procedure specification are owned by AutomVoj a.d. data.title: Distinguishing Learning from Guessing in Browser-Based Math Games: A Clickstream Modelling Proposal
data.markdown:
## The problem
Teachers using Zrenjanin Game Works' primary-school math games cannot distinguish a child who is learning from one who is clicking fast and guessing, despite having detailed timestamped clickstream logs for roughly 4,200 students over two school years (C002-CH1). Simple accuracy thresholds fail; a teacher confirmed a 91%-score student understood nothing when tested on paper.

## Research questions
1. Which features derived from timestamped click sequences best discriminate random guessing from deliberate, knowledge-based responding?
2. Can a Hidden Markov Model be reliably trained to identify latent 'learning states' from in-game clickstreams without requiring paper-test ground truth for every student?
3. What is the minimum interaction length required to flag a likely-guessing student with a false-positive rate acceptable to classroom teachers?

## Plan
| Year | Work | Result |
|------|------|--------|
| 1 | Ingest and explore the full 4,200-student CSV data; co-create a teacher-annotated ground-truth subset; engineer behavioural features from response times, attempt trails, and correctness sequences; train baseline classifiers with a target recall ≥ 0.75 on held-out data. | A descriptive report on guessing behaviours, a novel feature set, a validated baseline classifier, and a small annotated dataset. |

data.namedPublication: Applying Hidden Markov Models to Detect Shifts in Student Learning States from Clickstream Data
data.candidate: A PhD candidate with a strong MSc in computer science, statistics, or data science, demonstrable proficiency in Python or R, and prior coursework or project experience in machine learning and probabilistic graphical models. Familiarity with educational data or log-file analysis is highly desirable.
researchQuestions: 1. Which features derived from timestamped click sequences (e.g., response time distributions, answer-switching patterns, burst-of-speed episodes) best discriminate random guessing from deliberate, knowledge-based responding?

2. Can a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) be reliably trained to identify latent 'learning states' (e.g., focused, guessing, slipping) from in-game clickstreams without requiring paper-test ground truth for every student?
3. What is the minimum interaction length (number of question attempts) required to flag a likely-guessing student with a false-positive rate acceptable to classroom teachers?

plan.work: Data ingestion, exploratory analysis of the full 4,200-student CSV dataset, and definition of a ground-truth subset. Engineer candidate behavioural features from clickstreams (time-per-attempt, attempt trails, correctness patterns). Implement baseline classifiers (logistic regression, random forest) to distinguish teacher-validated guessers from known learners. Achieve first-iteration model with recall ≥ 0.75 on hold-out set.
plan.result: A descriptive report of guessing behaviours, a novel engineered feature set, and a validated baseline model with performance metrics. A small annotated ground-truth dataset co-created with at least two teachers.

plan.work: Develop and train a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to model latent student states over sequences of question attempts. Compare HMM state assignments against teacher-created ground truth and the baseline classifiers. Iteratively refine the model structure (number of states, emission distributions) using cross-validation on the Zrenjanin data. Design a lightweight output-conversion script that translates HMM state sequences into a simple, interpretable 'guessing likelihood' flag per student.
plan.result: A validated HMM for identifying latent learning/guessing states, a comparative evaluation against baseline models, and a prototype Python script that generates teacher-facing flags from raw CSV logs.

plan.work: Integrate the model into a small, offline testable tool. Conduct a structured field trial with teachers in 3–5 classrooms during the first half of the 2025–26 school year. Measure teacher agreement with model flags, tune the false-positive rate, and create documentation and a short teacher guide. Prepare the tool and methodological findings for publication.
plan.result: A polished, documented, and teacher-tested diagnostic tool ready for Zrenjanin Game Works deployment. Two journal papers submitted, covering the feature engineering and the HMM application in a K–12 game-based setting.

company: Complete, timestamped clickstream CSV logs for approximately 4,200 students across two school years (C002-CH1).
Direct access to teachers, classrooms, and schools in Vojvodina for iterative validation, ground-truth annotation, and a final field trial (C002-CH1).
Domain expertise in game-pedagogy and user-interface constraints from co-founders Tatjana and Miroslav Kovačević (C002-CH1).
Mirolsav Kovačević is available for roughly one day per week for research-related work (C002).
faculty: Supervisory expertise in educational data mining, sequence clustering, and Hidden Markov Model application to clickstream data (SYN-PUB-10455, SYN-PUB-10456).
Advanced statistical modelling skills, including logistic regression, mixed-effects survival analysis, and competency prediction (SYN-PUB-10454, SYN-PUB-06872).
A track record of translating LMS log data into actionable student-performance predictors (SYN-PUB-10454, SYN-PUB-10456).
Access to a pool of MSc-level students in data science and informatics for potential internship support on data engineering tasks (R1006).

data.whyThisPair: Zrenjanin Game Works possesses a rare, real-world dataset of 4,200 primary-school clickstreams with a verified problem of distinguishing guessing from mastery—but lacks in-house statistical modelling capacity. Prof. Mitrović has directly relevant published work on applying Hidden Markov Models to detect shifts in student learning states from clickstream data (SYN-PUB-10456), along with complementary expertise in sequence clustering (SYN-PUB-10455) and competency prediction (SYN-PUB-06872). This project offers a direct path from an established academic method to a practical, testable tool for teachers in a real multilingual school system, with a built-in field-trial window before the 2025–26 school year.

agreedUpFront.ip: Zrenjanin Game Works d.o.o. retains full ownership of its game platforms, clickstream datasets, and any integrated diagnostic tool. The University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, retains unrestricted ownership of the generalisable methods, models, and open-source reference implementations developed during the project. Either party may publish scientific findings derived from the methods, subject to the review period.

risks: The clickstream data may lack sufficient temporal density (e.g., students play only sporadically), leading to sparse sequences that prevent reliable HMM training and state differentiation.
Teachers may be unable or unwilling to provide the ground-truth annotations (paper-test verification) required to calibrate supervised models and validate the HMM's guessing states.
unverified: The precise volume and temporal granularity of the full 4,200-student CSV export, and whether it covers the same students over consecutive school years or unique cohorts.
The specific timeline and availability of teachers for the annotation work in Year 1 and the field trial in Year 3.
Whether the games currently use fixed question banks that would allow modelling of item-specific difficulty and discrimination parameters.
